To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the location privacy issues are a complex matter and should be addressed by taking into account the users’ social and location attributes, and the privacy issues related to location-based social networks.

(i) users’ socio-spatio attributes, such as gender and age, can be inferred from their online location attributes; (ii) users’ social attributes are correlated with their online location attributes, and (iii) the correlation between users’ social and location attributes varies according to the location precision level.

the social media user’s privacy is at risk due to the disclosure of his/her location information and that there is a need for the development of new location privacy attributes in order to protect the user’s privacy.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following: (i) identifying the social attributes of users through examining their location attributes while online; (ii) proposing a targeted set of privacy attributes that can be considered for the design and development of privacy-aware location sharing applications; and finally, (iii) providing a framework for the evaluation of the proposed location privacy attributes in the context of social media.
the privacy implications of the use of location-based services (LBS), which can be used to identify a user’s social identity attributes and thus to infer their social and behavioral affiliations.

identifying the location attributes that can be used for inferring users’ social characteristics and their privacy concerns, and to propose a new set of privacy attributes related to social media location information.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
location information is a very sensitive information that needs to be handled carefully.
the social media users’ privacy is not only about the location, but it is about the location and its social implications.
users’ social attributes are a significant part of users’ location privacy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are able to show that location information can provide information about a user’s social attributes and thus can lead to privacy leaks.
we have identified a number of location attributes that can be used to infer users’ social characteristics, which can be used to identify users’ social affiliations.

we are trying to address location privacy issues in social media by exploring the overlapping between location and social attributes in order to identify users’ social attributes while online, through examining their location attributes, and to provide a comprehensive list of location privacy attributes that are related to the users’ socio-spatio characteristics.
The main takeaway from our work is that
users can be identified based on their online location-sharing behavior and the social attributes that are associated with their location information.
the proposed set of attributes can serve as an initial step toward the identification of location privacy issues within LSAs and the specification of location privacy policies that can address them.
location-sharing applications can reveal users’ socio-spatio-temporal characteristics and affiliations with other users.
